subject: Threshold smoothing & overage sculpting for Hosted API commit tiers
body:
From: Jamal Thompson <jamal@everlyhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — baseline vs burst / min spend question

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. A couple of questions came up in our procurement sync around how Redwood structures minimums and overage rates for Hosted API (per-token) when we have a predictable baseline but frequent short spikes.

Quick context: we expect a steady baseline of ~1.2B tokens/month for the MVP, with occasional daily spikes that can be 2–3x baseline for 10–30 minutes. Procurement wants to avoid a large committed spend unless we can get a clear smoothing mechanism and a cap on instantaneous burst costs.

Can you share:
- A recommended commit tier for this profile and the per-token discount off list.
- How you price on-demand over-commit usage (flat multiplier? graduated?).
- Options for limiting burst exposure (hard caps, auto-fallback to lower-cost models, smoothing credits, monthly true-up).

We also attached our SOW template for your legal review (procurement_sow_v3.pdf).

Thanks,
Jamal
Director of Product
Everly Health

------------------------------------------------------------
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Thompson <jamal@everlyhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:28 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — baseline vs burst / min spend question

Hi Jamal — really appreciate the detail. Quick summary and a couple of options to consider below; attaching a model that maps your 1.2B baseline to several commit/overage structures (everly_mvp_commit_model.xlsx).

Short answer: we can architect a commit + smoothing arrangement that limits burst bill shock while keeping unit economics strong. The trade-offs are between (A) a higher commit with lower unit price and larger up-front commitment vs (B) a lower commit plus defined overage multipliers and smoothing credits.

Option A — Anchor commit (recommended if you can commit >= 75% of forecast)
- Baseline commit: 900M tokens/mo at $0.00032/token (≈32% off list for hosted).
- On-demand over-commit: billed at 1.6x the commit rate by default (i.e. $0.000512/token).
- Soft-burst window: first 40% above baseline per day billed at 1.9x with automatic smoothing credit applied monthly.
- Monthly true-up and a quarterly rebate if actuals exceed committed baseline by >20% sustained.

Option B — Lower commit + sculpted overage
- Baseline commit: 500M tokens/mo at $0.00036/token.
- Overage: tiered multipliers: 0–20% over = 1.9x, 20–50% = 2.2x, >50% = 2.6x.
- Cap on instantaneous spike exposure: we can agree a per-minute burst cap and an automatic fallback to a cost-optimized model when the cap is reached.

Operational controls we recommend
- Monthly true-up (standard).
- Smoothing credits that offset X% of short, infrequent spikes (applied at month-end).
- Optional pre-warm / reserved burst pool for predictable daily spikes (priced as a small add-on).

Next steps: Ben and Karthik are on copy to confirm whether we can bend the overage multipliers and propose an introductory concession for Q1. If needed, we can draft a short appendix to your SOW that defines caps and the true-up mechanism.

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min call later this week if you want to run numbers live.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai

------------------------------------------------------------
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Jamal Thompson <jamal@everlyhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — baseline vs burst / min spend question

Thanks Jamal / Stephanie — wrote up a couple of pragmatic variations. Attached is a worked example that applies your 1.2B forecast against both Option A & B (everly_mvp_commit_model.xlsx). Key callouts: 

- We can offer a Q1 introductory concession: reduce the overage multiplier by 0.1x for the first 90 days if Everly signs a 12-month commit. That effectively makes the early overage band 1.5–2.1x depending on banding.
- True-up cadence: monthly invoice + 30-day adjustment window.
- Burst cap enforcement: we can implement a per-minute or per-5-minute cap and automatically route excess to a lower-cost model variant (with a 40–50% unit-cost reduction). This mitigates instantaneous bill shocks.
- Legal/Procurement request: we generally push to avoid flat rebate guarantees; instead we prefer an operational rebate (sustained usage rebate) tied to actual monthly usage over runway.

Action items for Everly procurement: confirmation whether a 12-month commercial term is acceptable with the Q1 concession and whether you need a per-minute burst cap in the contract appendix.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

------------------------------------------------------------
From: Ariya Patel <ariya@synthex.co>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamal Thompson <jamal@everlyhealth.com>, procurement@everlyhealth.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:22:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — baseline vs burst / min spend question

Thanks for the clarity. A couple of procurement-specific asks from our side: 

1) We cannot accept a 12-month minimum unless there is a monthly true-up AND a firm cap on instantaneous burst cost exposure — procurement does not want a runaway invoice after a misconfig or traffic surge.
2) Can Redwood commit to a clear arithmetic formula for smoothing credits (not just a commitment to apply credits)? We prefer a formula such as: smoothing_credit = min( baseline * 0.15, total_spike_tokens * 0.6 ) applied at month-end.
3) If there is a quarterly rebate for sustained overage, we need the threshold and lookback window written into the SOW (e.g., sustained >20% for two consecutive months triggers rebate calculation).

Also looping in our security lead — they will need to start the SOC2 questionnaire soon.

Regards,
Ariya Patel
Head of Procurement (advisor to Everly)
ariya@synthex.co

------------------------------------------------------------
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Thompson <jamal@everlyhealth.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — threshold smoothing & overage sculpting for Hosted API commit tiers

Jamal / Ariya — appreciate the level of specificity. Agree we should put deterministic formulas into the SOW appendix so procurement has something explicit to sign. Proposed commercial terms (summarized):

- Baseline commit: 750M tokens/mo at $0.00034/token (signed 12-mo term).
- Smoothing credit formula (deterministic): smoothing_credit = min( baseline * 0.15, total_spike_tokens * 0.6 ). Credit is applied at month-end against overage charges.
- Overage bands (applied after smoothing credit):
  * 0–20% over baseline: 1.7x baseline rate
  * 20–50% over baseline: 2.1x baseline rate
  * >50% over baseline: 2.5x baseline rate
- Soft-burst protection: automatic per-minute cap of 35% of baseline (configurable). If cap hit, requests are routed to a cost-optimized fallback model variant (explicit in appendix).
- Quarterly sustained usage rebate: if monthly usage > baseline by 20% for two consecutive months, customer receives a rebate equal to 5% of that quarter's committed spend.
- True-up: monthly invoicing with a 30-day reconciliation; net settlement on next invoice.

Operational notes (for Redwood ops/legal)
- Need an SOW appendix with the smoothing formula, cap enforcement mechanism, and an explicit fallback-model mapping.
- Legal to review the procurement_sow_v3.pdf and confirm acceptable language for a 60-day ramp clause (customer can reduce committed baseline by up to 20% in first 60 days without penalty).

If Everly agrees we can convert this into redlined SOW language and route to your procurement. From our side, Ben will provide the final pricing workbook and I can draft the appendix language for legal to review.

Next steps / action items:
- Everly: confirm whether a 12-month term with 60-day ramp and the smoothing formula is acceptable (Jamal / Ariya).
- Redwood: Ben to share final workbook (done), Karthik to draft SOW appendix, Stephanie to schedule follow-up call.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
